label: rem:decuplet-equal-spacing
title: The decuplet equal-spacing rule has no discriminating power
html:
Remark. The decuplet equal-spacing rule has no discriminating power

The eightfold way's signature triumph was Gell-Mann's 1962 prediction of the \Omega^-. Within the baryon decuplet the consecutive mass differences

  \mathfrak{m}(\Sigma^*) - \mathfrak{m}(\Delta), \qquad
  \mathfrak{m}(\Xi^*) - \mathfrak{m}(\Sigma^*), \qquad
  \mathfrak{m}(\Omega) - \mathfrak{m}(\Xi^*)

are observed to be nearly equal, so the mass of the then-undiscovered \Omega^- could be read off from the three lighter states. The particle was found in 1964 within 0.6\% of the extrapolated value.

The rule carries no information about the breaking mechanism. This is a theorem, machine-checked sorry-free in QOU/Eightfold/DecupletEqualSpacing.lean: the three spacings are all equal for every choice of the first-order octet-breaking parameters a, b, c, over any commutative ring. Their common value is -4b - 6c, and the second difference vanishes identically (second_difference_vanishes). Two arbitrarily different breaking patterns therefore give the same answer (equal_spacing_cannot_discriminate).

Why the rule collapses

The Gell-Mann--Okubo mass operator is quadratic in the hypercharge,

  \mathfrak{m}(I, Y) = a + bY + c\left(I(I+1) - \tfrac{Y^2}{4}\right).

On the decuplet, and only because of the decuplet's own weight structure, the isospin is an affine function of the hypercharge:

State Y I 2I Y + 2
\Delta +1 3/2 3 3
\Sigma^* 0 1 2 2
\Xi^* -1 1/2 1 1
\Omega -2 0 0 0

Substituting 2I = Y + 2 collapses the quadratic term to a linear one,

  I(I+1) - \tfrac{Y^2}{4} = \tfrac{3Y + 4}{2},

so \mathfrak{m} is affine in Y (casimir_collapses_of_isospin_affine). Consecutive decuplet states step by \Delta Y = -1, hence the mass steps are equal. The \Omega is not an independent output at all: identically in a, b, c,

  \mathfrak{m}(\Omega) = 2\,\mathfrak{m}(\Xi^*) - \mathfrak{m}(\Sigma^*),

which means the extrapolation reads off a value the ansatz has already fixed (omega_eq_two_xi_minus_sigma).

The collapse is special to the decuplet, not generic. On the baryon octet the isospin is not even a function of the hypercharge --- \Sigma and \Lambda share Y = 0 with I = 1 and I = 0 --- so no such substitution exists and the argument has nothing to act on (octet_casimir_not_function_of_hypercharge, derived from the octet weight data rather than asserted). Without that contrast the result above could be misread as a fact about every \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} multiplet.

What this means for the framework

The same conclusion as the meson mass-splitting remark reaches for Gell-Mann--Okubo, and for the same structural reason. Equal spacing is a consequence of the form of the breaking --- octet, first order --- and not of any dynamics realising that form. Reproducing it would therefore be no evidence for this framework, or for any other. It is recorded here so that it is not later counted as one.

The testable content is the deviation. Measured spacings, as comparators only:

Spacing Value (MeV)
\Sigma^* - \Delta 152.6
\Xi^* - \Sigma^* 148.8
\Omega - \Xi^* 139.1

The spread is 13.6 MeV, about 9.2\% of the mean --- comparable to the \approx 6\% Gell-Mann--Okubo deviation on the pseudoscalar octet, and measuring the same thing: the failure of first-order breaking. The framework has derived no second-order term and so predicts a spread of 0. A derivation that produced \approx 9\% would be a genuine prediction; one that produced a materially different value would falsify the mechanism.

Nothing here is fitted, and nothing is wired to any computation.
